nodes.label: Next.js App Router icon.svg File Convention
nodes.norm_label: next.js app router icon.svg file convention

nodes.label: Custom Admin Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Payload's default dashboard is replaced with tiles grouped 'Edit the website' and 'Settings' plus plain-English hints, so staff never have to learn Payload's collections-vs-globals vocabulary. Lives in src/components/admin/Dashboard.tsx and Graphics.tsx with the theme in src/app/(payload)/custom.scss.

nodes.label: Daily VACUUM INTO Backup
nodes.rationale: VACUUM INTO is safe to run while the site is serving; keeps the last 14 copies (BACKUP_KEEP) next to the app, but backups/ must be synced off-box to survive losing the disk itself.

nodes.label: Service-in-City Combo Pages
nodes.rationale: 36 pages, every service x every city; adding a service or city in the CMS auto-creates its page, its combo pages, sitemap entries and internal links so staff never touch code for SEO landing pages.

nodes.label: Combo-Page Placeholder Template
nodes.rationale: One editable template with {service},{city},{state},{phone},{arrival},{price}; an unknown placeholder is left visible rather than silently blanked so typos are obvious. Unticking 'Generate these pages' removes all 36 at once.

nodes.label: Default Admin Credentials
nodes.rationale: admin@888lockandkey.com / ChangeMe123! is a known default that must be changed immediately, either in Admin -> Users or via SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL / SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD before seeding.

nodes.label: Drafts and Version History
nodes.rationale: Services, Locations and Pages keep the last 20 versions; every public query filters to published only so an unfinished edit cannot leak live. Enquiries and images deliberately have no drafts — a lead is a record of fact, not a document with revisions.

nodes.label: Enquiries Collection
nodes.rationale: Not publicly readable because it holds customer names and phones. Deletion is permanent with no recycle bin, available to any signed-in staff; can be locked to admins (delete: adminOnly in src/collections/Enquiries.ts) or replaced with the Closed status to keep the record.

nodes.label: /api/enquiry Form Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Forms post here instead of straight to Payload so the endpoint can validate and strip privileged fields a customer must not set (status, notes).

nodes.label: Honeypot Spam Field
nodes.rationale: A hidden field answering 200 so bots never learn they were caught; chosen over a captcha to avoid friction for real customers.

nodes.label: Lead Alert Emails
nodes.rationale: A new enquiry sends two isolated emails so one failing cannot stop the other: dispatcher alert (name, phone, service, city, message, one-tap Call, record link) and a customer confirmation with no admin link, sent only if the optional email field was filled. Sent on creation only so status changes do not re-notify. Never blocks a submission — the lead is saved and failures are logged with customer details so they can be recovered.

nodes.label: New Enquiries Banner
nodes.rationale: The only time-critical thing in the CMS, so it sits at the very top: turns orange with a count, links to unanswered leads and lists the five most recent with name, service, city, phone and age.

nodes.label: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL
nodes.rationale: Baked in at build time into sitemap, canonicals, robots and JSON-LD; if unset before the production build every URL points at localhost:3000.

nodes.label: src/lib/notify.ts Notification Hook
nodes.rationale: Single hook where a second alert channel drops in beside the email call.

nodes.label: Branded Password Reset Email
nodes.rationale: Why the email adapter matters: without it Payload writes the reset link to the server console and staff who forget their password are locked out.

nodes.label: payload migrate on npm start
nodes.rationale: Production has dev-push disabled and would otherwise boot with no schema, so `npm start` runs migrations from src/migrations/ before the server so a fresh database is built on first boot.

nodes.label: Placeholder Business Details
nodes.rationale: Everything shipped — (408) 555-0888, BSIS #LCO-000000, invented addresses — is placeholder and must be replaced under Settings -> Site settings and Locations.

nodes.label: In-Memory IP Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: 5 submissions per IP per 10 minutes counted in memory: resets on restart and is per-instance, the right trade for a single server. Move the counter to the database if it ever runs on more than one instance.

nodes.label: Admin and Editor Roles
nodes.rationale: Editors get content only and cannot create users or change roles, enforced at field level specifically so an editor cannot promote themselves.

nodes.label: Seed Starter Content
nodes.rationale: npm run seed wipes content and reloads starter content but keeps users, so reseeding never locks anyone out.

nodes.label: Sitemap, robots and JSON-LD Generation
nodes.rationale: app/robots.ts must stay at the app root — inside a route group it 404s. Sitemap includes the combo pages.

nodes.label: Single Source Phone Number
nodes.rationale: The phone number lives in one place (Settings -> Site settings) and feeds the header, hero, every CTA, the footer and the JSON-LD, so a change never has to be made in six places.

nodes.label: SMTP Email Configuration
nodes.rationale: One provider-agnostic SMTP setup in .env serves both lead alerts and password resets. With SMTP unset emails are rendered and logged instead of sent, so local development works and nothing disappears silently.

nodes.label: StickyCall.tsx Mobile Call Button
nodes.rationale: Hides itself whenever a real call button is on screen so the two are never stacked; any new prominent call button opts in with data-call-cta. The header pill, footer link and inline address numbers are deliberately unmarked, being too small to replace it.

nodes.label: Test Suite
nodes.rationale: Covers combo-page placeholders, lead alerts and password reset. The email test stubs the transport so it proves messages are built and sent without a mail provider, and also checks customer input is escaped and that editing a lead does not re-notify the dispatcher.

nodes.label: /thank-you Confirmation Page
nodes.rationale: noindex and kept out of the sitemap so it cannot rank or pollute analytics; it is the intended hook point for conversion tracking.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: Auto-generated marker block written and re-added by `next dev`; removing it from a diff only recreates the uncommitted change, so committing it with the work keeps the tree clean.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md Include of AGENTS.md
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is a one-line `@AGENTS.md` include so the agent rules live in a single file shared across tools.

nodes.label: 888 Lock & Key Website + CMS
nodes.rationale: One Next.js 16 App Router app serves both the public static site and the Payload 3 admin at /admin, avoiding a second deployable.

nodes.label: src/ Directory Structure
nodes.rationale: app/(payload)/ is generated and must not be edited; lib/ holds React-cached data access, JSON-LD and the template filler.

nodes.label: Next.js Version Diverges From Training Data
nodes.norm_label: next.js version diverges from training data
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes in APIs, conventions and file structure, so an agent must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code instead of trusting memorized conventions; docs resolve relative to AGENTS.md because in monorepos `next` may not be visible from the repo root.

nodes.label: Labelled Log Out Button
nodes.rationale: Payload's own log-out is an unlabelled sidebar icon staff could not find, so a labelled button naming the signed-in user was added and the sidebar item labelled too.

nodes.label: Persistent Disk Requirement
nodes.rationale: 888.db and media/ live on disk, so hosts with ephemeral filesystems (Vercel, Cloudflare Pages) would lose the database and uploads on redeploy; Railway, Render, Fly.io or a VPS are required.

nodes.label: Dev Server Port Fallback Gotcha
nodes.rationale: If 3000 is taken Next silently starts on 3001, so you can end up looking at a stale server — check the port it prints.

nodes.label: Postgres Migration Path
nodes.rationale: Swapping sqliteAdapter for postgresAdapter in src/payload.config.ts is enough because the schema is generated either way — keeps SQLite's simplicity without locking the project in.

nodes.label: Sidebar Icons Keyed off #nav-* IDs
nodes.rationale: Icons are attached via the #nav-* ids Payload emits rather than baked into labels, because an emoji in a label leaks into page titles, breadcrumbs and the API. href selectors do not work: the current page's nav item renders as a <div> with no href. Enquiries is ordered first via the collections array in src/payload.config.ts because staff open it daily.

nodes.label: SMS Alerts (Not Built)
nodes.rationale: Email alone will not wake anyone at 2am; a Twilio-style second channel is the identified gap, dropping in beside the email call in src/lib/notify.ts.

nodes.label: Native <details>/<summary> FAQ Accordions
nodes.rationale: Using the native elements means keyboard support and find-in-page work without any JavaScript.

nodes.label: CSS Review Marquee
nodes.rationale: Two identical CSS tracks; pauses on hover and focus and stops entirely under prefers-reduced-motion for accessibility.
